clue.text: One of two crossings Madox stands between?

definitions.text: One of two crossings Madox stands between?

parts.words: One of two crossings Madox stands between
parts.note: the novelist ... Madox ... has his middle name Madox standing between two identical surnames, each also a word for a shallow river crossing

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a man named Madox planted between two crossing points.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow place where a river may be waded is a crossing, and the writer's surname is that same word.

clue.text: Carmen, possibly Latino, working satisfactorily?

parts.note: Bizet's Carmen is an example of an opera

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of Latino may be rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a Latin production of Carmen is running smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges LATINO into TIONAL after OPERA; Carmen stands for opera by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Something operational is in working order, functioning as it should.

clue.text: University medic run over outside Scottish town

indicators.note: outside says the run-over pair wraps around the university medic

parts.note: to dart is to run quickly
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical qualification
on can mean over, as in resting on top of

explanation.surface: A university doctor knocked down by a car on the edge of a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the run-over pair around the university medic. 'run over' looks like a road accident but is two separate synonyms; MB is a British medical degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbarton is a town on the Clyde in west-central Scotland.

clue.text: Basis of call girl's transport rejected with hesitation

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the call girl's transport is read backwards as one run

parts.note: tart is slang for a prostitute, with the possessive giving TARTS
a bus is a means of transport
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Somebody hesitantly turns down a ride offered by a call girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the whole call girl's transport backwards before the hesitation is added; 'call girl' is old slang here.
explanation.definitionFit: A substratum is an underlying layer, the foundation on which something rests.

clue.text: Declining to confess, holding something to write with

indicators.note: holding means the first word contains the second

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
ink is used in writing

explanation.surface: A suspect refusing to confess while clutching a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: SING holds INK: S(INK)ING. 'sing' is criminal slang for informing or confessing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinking means going down or falling off, the same as declining.

clue.text: How piracy or villainy may be practised, somehow!

definitions.text: How piracy or villainy may be practised
definitions.meaning: literally by means of a pirate (Captain Hook) or a villain (a crook)
by any means available, fair or foul

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means by any means at all, and literally names a pirate captain and a criminal.

clue.text: Gardening skill duke excluded from finest book

parts.note: top means the best or finest

indicators.note: excluded from says the duke's letter is removed from the book

parts.note: a diary is a book of daily records

explanation.surface: A duke left out of the best book on gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluded from' removes the duke's D from the book, leaving IARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Topiary is the art of clipping shrubs into shapes, a horticultural skill.

clue.text: It's used for seasoning bird, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: bird is British slang for a prison sentence, as in doing bird, meaning doing time

explanation.surface: Something seasoned with a bird, as a cook might tell it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' suggests poultry, but here it is British slang for time in prison; 'we hear' signals the soundalike herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a herb widely used to flavour food.

clue.text: Tie the knot? Well I never

definitions.meaning: an archaic exclamation of surprise, originally an oath by the Virgin Mary

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to wed, and is also an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise.

clue.text: Writing skill of graduate in state founder's joint

indicators.note: in places the graduate inside the founder's name

parts.note: William Penn founded Pennsylvania, so the founder's gives PENNS
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A graduate's handwriting skill, linked to the hip of a state's founder.
explanation.walkthrough: William Penn founded Pennsylvania; 'in' puts the graduate inside his possessive name.
explanation.definitionFit: Penmanship is the art or skill of handwriting.

clue.text: Proponent of logical positivism? Yes, right

parts.note: aye means yes

explanation.surface: Agreeing that logical positivism has a champion.
explanation.definitionFit: The philosopher A. J. Ayer was the leading British advocate of logical positivism.

clue.text: A wife in one state or another

indicators.note: in puts the article and the wife inside the first state

parts.note: Mali is a state in West Africa

explanation.surface: A married woman living in one country or another.
explanation.walkthrough: A and W go inside MALI: MAL(AW)I. 'another' stands for a second African state.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is another African country, so it is a different state from the first.

clue.text: Old park keeper's yen for fruit from here?

parts.note: a ranger looks after a park
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: An elderly park ranger longing for fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like longing, but it is the currency, giving Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glasshouse where citrus trees are grown, so citrus fruit comes from there.

clue.text: Immature weakling with a permanent way to secure money

indicators.note: to secure means the weakling holds the money inside

parts.note: a runt is the weakest of a litter
a dime is a US coin, a sum of money
the permanent way is the railway track, RY being the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A feeble person using a railway line to keep their money safe.
explanation.walkthrough: RUNT holds DIME: RU(DIME)NT, then A and RY. 'Permanent way' is the railway engineers' term for track.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudimentary means undeveloped or at an early stage, like something immature.

clue.text: Aromatic plant in perfect condition

definitions.meaning: a fragrant herb of the genus Mentha
as new, as in a coin or stamp in ... condition

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a fragrant herb and also means pristine, as new.

clue.text: Smugly virtuous couple from old TV trio

indicators.note: couple from means two of the trio's members are taken, so one name appears twice

parts.note: The Goodies were a British comedy trio on 1970s television, each member being one Goody

explanation.surface: A self-righteous pair drawn from a former television threesome.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goodies were a British TV comedy trio; two of them give GOODY twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A goody-goody is someone ostentatiously well behaved and self-righteous.

clue.text: Boy rustic's strange inconspicuousness

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of boy rustic are put in an unusual order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A country boy's odd lack of visibility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges BOYRUSTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscurity is the state of being unnoticed or unknown, being inconspicuous.

clue.text: Value Benin's output, receiving no appreciation

indicators.note: output is what is produced, so the letters of value and Benin are worked into something new

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Assessing what the African country of Benin produces, with no thanks given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'output' rearranges VALUEBENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unenviable is not wanted by anyone, attracting no envy or admiration.

clue.text: Soldier tossed up old coin in base

indicators.note: tossed up in a down clue means the soldier is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
the noble was an old English gold coin

explanation.surface: A soldier flipping an antique coin at the military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed up' turns GI into IG. 'base' looks like a camp, but means low or dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and ignoble both mean dishonourable or mean-spirited.

clue.text: Delight English circle in Belgian province

indicators.note: in places the circle inside the Belgian province

parts.note: Namur is a province of Belgium
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: An English social circle enjoying itself in a Belgian province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the circle inside the Belgian province; 'circle' is O by its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour is to charm or captivate, to delight someone.

clue.text: Declaration of total number who like it hot?

indicators.note: declaration means something spoken, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: sum means total

explanation.surface: Announcing how many people enjoy things hot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the film Some Like It Hot: the people who like it hot are 'some', an unspecified number.
explanation.definitionFit: Some is an indefinite number of people, as in the film title.

clue.text: European oil spillage almost engulfing river

indicators.note: engulfing means the shortened spillage surrounds the river
almost removes the final letter of the spillage word

parts.note: an oil slick is a spillage of oil on water
the Avon is a British river

explanation.surface: A European oil spill nearly swallowing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the spillage word to SLIC, which 'engulfing' then wraps around the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavonic means relating to the Slavs, a European people, or their languages.

clue.text: Charmer switching two of Thorndike's characters

indicators.note: switching two of means two letters of the name change places

parts.note: the actress Dame Sybil Thorndike; her characters are the letters of her first name

explanation.surface: Swapping two of an actress's stage roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching two of' exchanges the Y and I of SYBIL. 'characters' looks like stage roles but means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibyl is a prophetess, a woman supposed to wield magical powers, such as a sorceress or charmer.

clue.text: It may indicate a school for East Enders

indicators.note: Cockneys from London's East End traditionally drop the h at the start of words

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: Something pointing out a school for London's Cockneys.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a leading English private school; Cockney speech drops its H.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a sign used to point the way.

clue.text: Former pupils taking salt to part of UK

parts.note: alum is a double sulphate salt
NI is Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Old students bringing salt to Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumni are former students of a school or university.

clue.text: Tedious person's wave

definitions.meaning: a tidal wave surging up a river, as on the Severn

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a dull person and also a tidal surge up an estuary.

clue.text: Oddly, Briton's sound description of some detergents

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the following word

parts.note: logical means sound, as in a sound argument

explanation.surface: A Briton's odd-sounding account of washing powders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' picks B, I, O from Briton's.
explanation.definitionFit: Biological detergents contain enzymes, and the label is printed on their packets.

clue.text: Villain needs lawyer: there's professional opportunity for an unknown

indicators.note: for means the opportunity stands in place of the unknown

parts.note: taken as written
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra
a break is a chance for career advancement

explanation.surface: A criminal needs a lawyer, offering a newcomer a big chance.
explanation.walkthrough: BREAK replaces the Y of LAWYER: LAW-BREAK-ER. 'an unknown' looks like an obscure performer but is the algebraic Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawbreaker is a criminal, a wrongdoer or villain.

clue.text: Move up and down repeating president's greeting?

indicators.note: repeating means the greeting is said twice

parts.note: George W. Bush notoriously greeted Tony Blair with yo

explanation.surface: A president bobbing about while saying hello again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Recalls George W. Bush's 'Yo, Blair' greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To yo-yo is to fluctuate or move repeatedly up and down.
